name: Deep-drilled brine wells in Sichuan
summary: From about the mid-eleventh century, salt makers in Sichuan reached underground brine by deep drilling, a technique that was invented there.
description: In Sichuan, salt was made from underground brine that reached the surface in springs or was tapped through dug shaft wells. From the mid-eleventh century onwards the brine was also tapped by deep drilling, which the historian Hans Ulrich Vogel says was invented in this region. The same abstract notes that Sichuan salt makers boiled brine with natural gas, first recorded in the third century and used more systematically from the sixteenth.

impact.note: Scored partly on the general view, since the source is an abstract: drilled wells served the salt industry of one region (reach 1), gave it a new way to reach brine that the industry was then built around (depth 2), and are credited only with their successors among Sichuan's own brine and gas wells, because no link to drilling elsewhere is sourced (generativity 1).

date.label: from the mid-11th century CE
date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: In Sichuan, underground brine was tapped by deep drilling from the mid-eleventh century onwards, alongside springs and shaft wells.

evidence.supports: tapped with the help of shaft wells and, in Sichuan from the mid-eleventh century onwards, by deep-drilling

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated evidence found for this capability in this community. No review has yet confirmed that nothing earlier exists.

unresolved.note: Re-cite Vogel's abstract or chapter from the publisher's edition (Presses universitaires de Franche-Comté, on OpenEdition Books), which refused the fetcher; the page cited here is a bibliography entry on a private website that reproduces the abstract and truncates the chapter title.
The lead's 1041-1048 CE, the percussion bit and the bamboo cable and casing need a source; Vogel's fuller studies of the Sichuan wells were not reached.
Depths reached over time, including the Shenhai well (1835, about 1,001 m), need an academic or primary source; only popular pages were found.
The Han-period dug shaft wells need a source that separates them from the later drilled wells.
Whether knowledge of Chinese drilling reached Europe or America before nineteenth-century brine and oil drilling is unchecked (Needham was not reached).

research.note: Vogel states that Sichuan is the region where deep drilling for salt was invented; the abstract does not compare it with early drilling elsewhere.
